findings.fix: Name the entity that created the component. Exactly one. For open source, use the package manager's convention where one exists, otherwise the original project or maintaining organization. If there is genuinely no clear producer, state unknown provenance explicitly.
findings.severityJustification: This element replaces Supplier Name and exists to give a point of contact for security concerns and to disambiguate same-named components from different producers. Measurement across 10,000 repositories found zero percent of generated SBOMs carry it, so this rule will fire on almost every real file, which is the point.

findings.fix: Record the hash of the executable component artifact as ASCII hexadecimal. If the artifact was not available, state that the value is unknown.
findings.severityJustification: A hash is what lets a recipient verify they hold the same artifact the SBOM describes. The document permits 'unknown' when the author had no access to the executable artifact, which is legitimate for a before-build SBOM, so this rule accepts an explicit unknown and fires only on silence.

findings.severityJustification: This is the element the whole matching layer depends on. Without an identifier a component cannot be looked up in any vulnerability database, which is precisely the failure that produces an FDA information request. Escalated to error in the FDA pack, where a named downstream consequence justifies it.

findings.fix: Make the SBOM available promptly to those who need it, through a version-specific URL, an API, or alongside installation. Access controls may limit who sees it but should not block authorized parties or prevent integration into trusted security tools.
findings.severityJustification: Mostly an organizational practice. The file-level signal is whether it carries a version-specific reference a recipient could return to.
findings.sourceRef: cisa-2026-v2.1: Practices and Processes, 3, Distribution and Delivery (Minor Update)
findings.title: Distribution and delivery: the document is retrievable at a stable reference

findings.fix: Where a field is not provided, state whether the information is unknown to you or withheld by you. Have a process for recipients to ask about redacted security-related information.
findings.severityJustification: The highest-leverage practice in the document and the one most often ignored. The distinction it draws is between information unknown to the author and information the author is withholding, and a reader is entitled to know which. A field left empty tells them neither.
findings.sourceRef: cisa-2026-v2.1: Practices and Processes, 4, Explicitly Identifying Unknown Information (Major Update)
findings.title: Explicitly identifying unknown information: gaps are stated, not silent

findings.fix: Generate a new SBOM for every build or release, and reissue a revised one when you discover new details or correct an error.
findings.severityJustification: Each software version should have its own SBOM. A file-level proxy is whether the document names the exact component version it describes, so a consumer can tell which build it belongs to.
findings.sourceRef: cisa-2026-v2.1: Practices and Processes, 5, Frequency (Minor Update)
findings.title: Frequency: the document is bound to a specific component version
